AR-11.note: Backups of the whole sidebar (Spaces, each profile’s Favorites, pinned and Today tabs, folders, split views; no private profiles) in userData/backups, one JSON file each: taken within 5 minutes of a sidebar change (only when it differs from the newest; browsing alone never makes one), once 30 s after launch, before every restore, and with Back Up Now. Kept: the newest 10 of today, then the newest of each of the 10 days before, of each week of the month before that and of each 30 days of the year before that; a deleted profile’s Favorites, Spaces and tabs are taken out of every backup. Help → Restore Data… (macOS) and the command bar open the Backups section of the Library: a dated list (day headings, time, Spaces and tabs; a file that can’t be read is listed as such, without Restore); Restore… asks first, then puts the sidebar back: tabs in both keep their page, tabs only in the backup come back asleep (with the page and history the Archive kept for them, leaving the Archive), tabs opened since go to the Archive, Spaces added since go; private windows and their tabs are left alone; Favorites over 12 go to Today (D33). When the sidebar can’t be backed up first, nothing changes. A running import stops first: none of the tabs it hasn’t shown yet go to the Archive, and its window says why (D65). Each restore is one step on the sidebar’s undo stack (TB-18): the toast’s Undo or ⌘Z, also in the Library, puts back the sidebar it replaced, a second ⌘Z goes further back and ⌘⇧Z restores again; earlier steps stay. After an undo, a window moved off a removed Space stays where it went, and the pages come back asleep

Programs, installers, scripts and disk images wait under their partial name with Keep / Discard in the sidebar row, the Library and the flyout, through a restart too: everywhere exe, msi, dmg, pkg, deb, rpm, AppImage, .desktop launchers, sh/bash/zsh/py/pl/rb scripts, iso/img/vhd/vhdx, jar, jnlp, apk…; on Windows also its own script, shortcut and system types (js, vbs, wsf, hta, lnk, url, scf, settingcontent-ms, chm, reg, inf, msc, dll…). Keep puts the file in place and marks it, Discard deletes it. Every such file is held, whatever the site, as there is no reputation service. Gap, by the spec's own rule (D54): Safe Browsing, which needs a reputation service; none is free to use (Google's is non-commercial, Web Risk is paid)

DL-13.note: PDFs (the engine's viewer), raster pictures, plain text, audio and video open in a tab (only types that run no script there, D53: a downloaded SVG opens in its app); a site that sends the file as an attachment still downloads it (DL-01); the PDF viewer's download button saves through the usual download flow (row, Library, DL-02 flight). Missing: offering Orbit as Windows' app for local .pdf files (Settings → General, P2), which finish-settings builds (D54): the installer's file association and opening files passed on the command line

DL-14.note: Windows/Linux: Ctrl+J opens the downloads flyout at the top left, beside the sidebar (Orbit has no top toolbar): the 12 newest with live progress, Keep/Discard, Resume/Retry/Cancel and Show in Folder; a click opens a file, rows drag out (DL-06), Show All opens the Library's Downloads section; Esc, Ctrl+J again or a click outside closes it. macOS: ⌘⇧J and ⌥⌘L open the Library's Downloads section (KS-12). The command bar has a "Downloads" action

ST-01.note: own window (⌘, / Ctrl+,): opens or focuses one; remembers section and size; takes the opener Space's colours; sections come from a registry (src/renderer/src/settings/registry.ts); search filters rows

Not built: UP-04's install-while-idle, hover-preview toggles (OT-26, P2), Open PDFs (P2)

OB-02.note: audit and e2e: no account UI anywhere, onboarding included; a first run sends nothing off the computer, with or without onboarding, except Chromium's spell-check dictionary download (see tests)

No HTTPS-first or Safe Browsing (not in Electron), no per-site clearing here

OB-01.note: a window of its own before any browser window on a first run (gated by settings.onboarded; e2e runs skip it unless ORBIT_ONBOARDING=1): Orbit's logo with the moon in motion (still with reduced motion), a welcome line, Get started; steps slide in (about 400 ms, none with reduced motion); Enter continues, Esc goes back; each step's title takes focus; progress dots are labelled. No sounds or music (optional), no haptics (Electron has no API), no first-window shimmer

OB-03.note: the import flow inline (IM-01 to IM-06): the browsers on this computer, several profiles allowed, the data types and the bookmark tree, a bookmarks file dropped or chosen, the paste route and the help for people moving from another browser, with Do this later weighing the same as Next. An import chosen there is read at once and added when Start browsing ends onboarding, where the Done screen sums it up; Skip setup adds nothing (D44). Letter tiles, not browser logos (as IM-02)

OB-04.note: the Space theme picker (same ThemeEditor) for the first Space, applied live, with a preview of sidebar and frame, grain and intensity; Light / Dark / Match system (Match system preselected, Continue works at once); says it can be changed later. No haptics

OB-05.note: 16 web apps as letter tiles (no logos fetched), nothing preselected, at most 12; they become the first Space's profile's Favorites, unloaded until opened. No ordering by imported history (no import yet)

OB-06.note: there is no ad and tracker blocker (OT-15), so the step is left out of the flow

OB-07.note: explains what the default browser does; Make Orbit my default and Not now with the same weight; on Windows says what to pick in Default apps; status asked again when the window comes back to the front; no reminders later. Test runs use a stub

OB-08.note: a Search with row on the Done screen: the Default profile's engine (ST-06's list), Google until changed

OB-09.note: Done screen sums up colours, Favorites, default browser and import (what will be added from where, e.g. "6 bookmarks from bookmarks.html", or that nothing was and where import lives); Start browsing (Back to browsing after a reset) opens the first window centred at about 86% of the screen with the colours and Favorites picked, command bar closed. No Orbit basics folder or local welcome tab (no local guide pages yet)

OB-14.note: Skip setup on every step but the last gives the spec's default first window: the theme step's colours and mode are undone and no Favorites are added (D44). The step, the theme and the Favorites picked so far are saved, so a quit part-way resumes there with them. An import chosen at the import step isn’t: it waits in memory for Start browsing, so a quit before then loses it, and the Done step says nothing was imported (it’s in Settings, under General); Reset Onboarding (command bar only) runs the flow again over the open windows and deletes nothing

IM-01.note: the import window (a child of the browser window, in its Space's colours): Back / Next / Cancel, Cancel at any step imports nothing, Enter is Next and Escape is Back, ⌘W closes it. Opened from onboarding (the same flow inline, OB-03), the command bar's Import from Another Browser, Settings → General → Import…, and on macOS the app menu's Import from Another Browser… (macOS-unverified). Not built: a ☰ entry on Windows/Linux (Orbit has no ☰ menu). In the progress view, Cancel is offered only while the source is read; once adding starts it offers Hide, and the bookmarks added are one undo step. The window isn’t modal: the browser window stays usable while it’s open, as IM-14 asks

IM-02.note: the browsers found on this computer (Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi, Opera, Opera GX, Firefox; Safari on macOS), each a tile in its colour with its profile or profile count; those not installed aren't shown. Several profiles: a step to choose one or more, by name. Profiles come from Chromium's Local State (or a single Default folder, or Opera's own folder) and Firefox's profiles.ini; every file is read from a copy. Safari without Full Disk Access is shown as blocked, with the way round it (export a bookmarks file from Safari and import that). Tests search only made-up fixture folders. Letter tiles, not logos: Orbit doesn't ship other browsers' marks. Safari's reader (Bookmarks.plist, a binary property list) is tested on fixtures, macOS-unverified

IM-03.note: after the source and its profiles, what they hold as checkboxes, all on, with counts ("6 bookmarks, as pinned tabs", "6 pages visited"); types a source can't provide aren't shown, and a profile whose file the browser holds offers the rest; never passwords or cards (D52). Cancel (Do this later in onboarding) weighs the same as Next. Extensions are listed, off, as not importable yet (IM-09). Cookies (IM-10) aren’t offered. A file that is there but can’t be read is named with why, e.g. “Work: history couldn’t be read (the file is damaged)”, and the profile’s other types are still offered

IM-06.note: the last step: the profile (it gets the history) and the Space (its pinned section gets the bookmarks): the current Space by default, the first one in onboarding, or New Space… with a name. Several source profiles: "Make a matching Orbit profile and Space for each" makes them, in order, named after the source profiles, each getting its own profile's history. Private windows' profiles aren't offered and never get history

IM-04.note: the source's tree (Chromium's bookmarks bar, other and mobile bookmarks; Firefox's toolbar, menu, other and mobile bookmarks; Safari's favorites bar, menu and reading list; a file's own groups), several profiles each under its name, with a checkbox per folder and bookmark; everything chosen at first; Select all / none; "4 of 6 bookmarks selected". Addresses that can't be pinned show unticked with the reason. Folders below the top level start closed, and so does a top-level one holding over 1,000 bookmarks. The list isn’t virtualized: every row at the top level or in an open folder is drawn, so a large file shows quickly only when its bookmarks sit in such closed folders (20,000 in folders of 2,000 show in about 0.4 s). 20,000 bookmarks at the top level take about 2.9 s to show; 200,000 there, or 200 top-level folders of 1,000, about 30 s; 10,000 top-level folders about 6 s; and opening a large folder draws all its rows. Only the import window waits

IM-05.note: one pinned folder "Imported from <Browser>" ("Imported bookmarks" from a file) at the end of the target Space's pinned section: the source's top-level groups and nested folders kept, in order, as closed sub-folders (the folder itself closed above 1,000 items); several profiles into one Space each get a sub-folder by name; each bookmark a pinned tab with its title and address, asleep, with no favicon or request until opened; bookmarklets, saved searches, browser-only and non-web addresses skipped and counted; Firefox tags and separators left out; no Favorites made; one undo step takes it all back. 2,000 bookmarks take about 0.3–0.4 s, made out of sight in parts and shown at once (IM-14), with the longest main-process stall about 40–50 ms. Not built: fetching a favicon when an imported row scrolls into view; its icon comes when the tab is first opened

IM-13.note: bookmarks HTML (the Netscape format; Chromium- and Firefox-style exports tested) and a .txt list of links, from From a file… or dropped on the import window or the sidebar. Bookmarks map as IM-05 into "Imported bookmarks"; links as IM-12 (a list over about 1 MB or 10,000 lines shows only its count and first lines); a file with neither says "No bookmarks found in this file" and imports nothing; a cut-off file imports what it holds. Files are read in a worker, in time linear in their size (D58): main’s longest stall is about 0.07 s for a 16 MB file or list, and about 0.2 s for a 60 MB file of 200,000 bookmarks. A file nested deeper than 64 folders keeps its deeper bookmarks in the 64th; a file gives at most 200,000 bookmarks (folders don’t count) and 20,000 folders, the bookmarks of folders past that kept in the folder that holds them; over 64 MB, every route, a paste included, says “This is too large to import (the limit is 64 MB)” without reading it; a read that fails says “Orbit couldn’t read this file”. No passwords CSV (D52)

IM-12.note: Paste a list of links (one address per line, "Title — address" with a dash, bar or tab, Markdown links, bullets): one pinned folder named by the user, a pinned tab per link in order, asleep; lines that aren't links are counted in the summary. ⌘V / Ctrl+V on the sidebar (outside a text field) with two or more links on the clipboard opens the same import with them filled in. A list over about 1 MB or 10,000 lines, pasted or from a file, isn’t put in the text field: the import window shows its count and first eight lines, read-only, with Clear, and imports it as it is. A paste over 64 MB as UTF-8 (22.5 million CJK characters, say) says “This is too large to import (the limit is 64 MB)”, as a file does, and none of it leaves the window it was pasted in. Clear also frees main’s copy of a held list. The other routes (a bookmarks file, notes, canvases, site styles) are explained in the import window's help, which reads nothing from another browser; passwords are out of scope (D52)

IM-14.note: progress per data type (a spinner, then a check), then a summary with counts per type and the skipped items with reasons; Done shows the imported folder in the sidebar (its Space, the pinned section open, the folder in view). Bookmarks are made out of sight, in parts, and their folder is shown whole, at once (D62): while 20,000 are added, the browser window’s longest freeze is under 0.1 s; 100,000 take about 34 s, with the window’s longest freeze about 0.34 s and main’s longest stall about 0.57 s (saving the state). A file the source browser holds (it can't be copied) shows "Chrome is using some of its files. Quit Chrome and try again, or import the rest" with Try again; the types it could read can still be imported. History shows the pages read, then added; Done says they're in History and the command bar; what History can't keep is listed with the reason. The summary lists every item left out with its reason: skipped bookmarks (also in a folder that holds nothing else), those past 200,000 bookmarks in one file, list or profile (folders don’t count, so the summary and the selection count agree), lines that aren’t links, and a profile’s file that couldn’t be read (“Work: history couldn’t be read (the file is damaged)”). Until the folder shows, nothing lists its tabs (D65): not the command bar (by title, by address or among recent tabs), the recent-tab switcher or the Library. One the user reached anyway and placed stays where they put it, and the folder leaves it out. A quit or a failure part-way takes back exactly the tabs the import made, by id, wherever they are, and nothing of the user’s; a crash part-way leaves none either, as the next start removes tabs that no section shows. Restore Data part-way stops the import first: its tabs are removed without going to the Archive, and the import window says “The import stopped: data was restored from a backup.” Copies of the other browser’s files go in a folder under Orbit’s user data, removed at quit (a copy still being made too) and cleared at startup (D58)

IM-07.note: Chromium's History, Firefox's places.sqlite and Safari's History.db (macOS-unverified), read from copies a window of rows at a time, into the chosen profile's history: each page with its title, visit and typed counts and its newest visits (up to 20). History (⌘Y / Ctrl+H) lists them and the command bar suggests and completes them at once; no tab is made and nothing loads. Left out: browsers' own pages, hidden pages, frame loads (Chromium subframes; Firefox embeds, framed links, downloads). History keeps the 50,000 most recent pages: a larger history keeps its newest and the summary counts the rest. 100,000 pages take about 2 s, with main's longest stall about 50–110 ms and none in the windows; the profile's history is written once, as a snapshot

IM-15.note: the same browser or file again makes a new "Imported from <Browser> (2)" folder (then (3)…), never merging into or changing the first. History de-duplicates silently: a page already imported gains only the visits it lacked, so its counts aren't doubled. Passwords aren't imported (D52)

IM-16.note: after onboarding's import of a history, the Done step offers the six sites visited most (each by its most-visited page, or its home page when that's a search): the first three as Favorites, the rest as pinned tabs. One click takes one (another takes it back); Dismiss all drops them. They're added unloaded with the import when Start browsing ends onboarding, never with Skip setup (D44). Orbit can't tell web apps from other sites, so it ranks by visits; a suggested pinned tab is named after its site until first opened

IM-17.note: Export Pinned Items as Bookmarks… in the File menu (macOS-unverified: Orbit has no menu bar elsewhere), the command bar, and Settings → General → Import and export (with Include Today tabs) writes a standard bookmarks HTML file through the system's save dialog: the Favorites a folder (one per profile when there are several), each Space a folder of its pinned section with its folders nested as they are, a split's tabs in its place; Today's tabs only when chosen, as a Today folder in their Space. Orbit's own pages and private windows' profiles are left out. Copy All Links on a folder is the tabs lane's (it exists)

IM-09.note: A Chromium-family profile's extensions are listed on the types step, from its Preferences and Secure Preferences (read from copies; a name kept only in the manifest is read from it, in its default language): pinned ones first, the browser's own left out. The row is off and says they aren't importable yet; unpacked ones never come over. Not built: installing them fresh from the store with one summary confirmation, pinning the pinned ones, and the ad-blocker de-duplication (blockers are already marked), because the extensions lane's install path isn't on main yet. Firefox add-ons aren't listed (the spec covers Chromium-family sources)

ST-11.note: Theme mode: Light / Dark / Match system (AP-01). Not built: window material (AP-10, Windows), app icon (AP-09), page defaults (P2)

ST-17.note: Settings → About: logo, version (a click copies it), build date, Chromium and Electron versions, system, Check for updates, release notes, Copy build info. Licence and Open-source credits open credits.html, built with the app (D43): Orbit's and Electron's licences, a link to the LICENSES.chromium.html Electron ships, and the licence of each npm package whose code ships. Release notes and help need access to the private repository for now

OB-13.note: command-bar Help, Report a Bug, What's New and Copy Build Info; macOS Help menu (Orbit Help, Report a Bug…, Release Notes, Troubleshooting → Copy Build Info). Help opens the project README; Report a Bug opens a new issue on the public tracker with the build info filled in. The shortcut sheet entry comes with OB-12 (keys lane)

UP-01.note: checks a release feed at launch (after 30 s) and about every 4 h ± 30 min, after wake if overdue; silent, failures retried at the next check; a private in-memory session that sends only Orbit's version, system and processor type (no cookies). Nothing is checked until a feed is set in Settings → General (empty by default; test and dev builds accept only a feed on this computer). Not built: background download (builds are unsigned, so UP-10's stub)

UP-02.note: sidebar banner above the Space switcher, in the Space's colours: a pill that opens on hover with a gradient button; ✕ hides it for 24 h or until the next launch. UP-10 form: "New version available" opens the release page in a tab; no relaunch until signed builds

UP-03.note: command bar and macOS app menu "Check for Updates…" open Settings → About (not a separate window) and check: Checking…, up to date, available, or the failure; Download opens the release page (UP-10); a click on the version copies it. Not built: download progress and Relaunch, the Turn on offer (UP-04), a ☰ entry on Windows/Linux

UP-06.note: after a version change the sidebar shows "Updated to Orbit X" with See what's new, which opens that version's GitHub release notes in a tab; ends when opened, dismissed or after 3 days; command bar "What's New" and Help → Release Notes. Not built: the release's one-line summary in the banner

UP-07.note: About Orbit (app menu) opens Settings → About: logo, version, engine, Electron, build date (set at build time), Copy build info, and the licence and open-source credits from a page that comes with the app (D43); Help → Troubleshooting → Copy Build Info and the command-bar action copy version, build date, engine, OS and processor

UP-10.note: reads Orbit's JSON feed ({version, url, summary, security}) or a GitHub releases API answer (latest, or a list: newest non-draft, non-pre-release); a newer version shows "New version available" and opens its page in a tab. No feed is set up yet: the address is empty by default

UP-12.note: a release marked [security] in its GitHub name or notes, or security: true in Orbit's feed, shows "Important security update" in the banner and Settings

FL-01.note: one token set in shared/motion.ts and motion.css (instant 90 ms, quick 130 ms, pop 240 ms; snappy, standard and pop springs), checked against each other by a unit test; interrupted motions turn round from where they are (Space slide, command bar, hover card, folders, ⌘S)

FL-04.note: row hover lights on the instant timing and fades out from where it is when the pointer leaves; every row a sweep enters lights

FL-05.note: a press selects the row in its frame, before the page shows (within 50 ms); a press on a row still growing in selects it

FL-06.note: a new row grows with the snappy spring, its content fading in over the last 60 %; the rows below glide

FL-07.note: pinned, unpinned or moved by key or menu: the row travels with the standard spring while the room it leaves and the room it takes close and open with it; to a place out of sight or another Space it collapses out in place and the list does not scroll; ⌘Z plays it back

FL-08.note: ×, audio and folder search buttons: circle fades in on the instant timing; the glyph presses to 0.9 at once and springs back (pop); the click fires on release and the row starts leaving within 2 frames (main closes the tab in between); the reset acts on press (PN-04)

FL-09.note: a closing row fades and slides 12 px while its room collapses with the snappy spring and the rows below rise; the next tab is selected in the same frame; rows out of sight go without motion

FL-10.note: a 4 px move lifts the row (1.03, shadow, 95 %) in that frame; the row is drawn under the pointer in every frame; Escape springs it back to its slot

FL-11.note: Clear sweeps the rows out one after another (25 ms apart, at most 12 staggered) within 450 ms; the divider and New Tab stay; ⌘Z brings them back in one group

FL-12.note: folders and the pinned section: the chevron turns in 160 ms; the box grows with the snappy spring while its rows fade in 12 ms apart (only when the user opens it); closing is quicker; reduced motion fades

FL-20.note: a new Favorite pops in from 0.85 with the pop spring while the other tiles re-flow with the snappy spring; a removed one shrinks to 0.85 and fades where it was while the grid closes up

FL-21.note: only the rows near the visible band are drawn; a Space shown for the first time draws a stand-in at once and its list within ~160 ms; on this machine under load a 200-tab fling and a 500-tab scroll still have a few frames of two intervals (5 and 12), so p99 is two intervals, against none over one (docs/FEEL.md)

FL-22.note: rise 12 px from 0.96 with the pop spring, at most three 8 px apart, a new one pushes the others up with the snappy spring, stays 3 s (4 s with a button), a hovered one with a button waits until 1 s after the pointer leaves; fade and 8 px drop in 160 ms. Shown at the bottom of the sidebar (not over the page card, so hidden behind the page when the sidebar is), plain toasts let clicks through, and no Space theme yet (AP-14)

FL-25.note: folder search and icon picker: drawn in the first frame, from 0.97 with the snappy timing (150 ms); close with the quick fade; keys go back to the sidebar at once

FL-28.note: follows the OS setting, with a setting to force it on (AP-17); springs, slides and scales become short fades or instant changes; drags still follow the pointer and settle with a short ease

FL-29.note: measured by the feel specs against each budget (docs/FEEL.md); press, ⌘W, ⌘S, Space switch (settles in ~290 ms), command bar and drag budgets met; still missed: p99 at two intervals in some animations under load (⌘S hide, long lists, a Peek opening), the hover sidebar and a Peek's close start in the second frame, and the first ⌘T after a launch can show in the second frame

FL-30.note: the nine points as a checklist in docs/FEEL.md: pass, gap or fixed, each with the test that shows it

FL-18.note: a tab dragged over the page: the zone fades in over 100 ms on the half the new pane takes and moves between halves at once; the new pane grows in from its side with the standard spring; the divider follows the pointer 1:1; flip and close travel with the spring (docs/FEEL.md); a tab dragged onto another tab row highlights the half (SV-05) but has no bubble preview or wobble on drop

FL-27.note: a resized window keeps the card's margin in every frame and the page view gets each width within a frame at the median (18 ms at worst), over the page's own colour; the OS full-screen transition; new windows open a step down and right (NV-10) with the command bar's entrance; an inactive window's sidebar dims over 150 ms and comes back at once on focus; no launch sheen (optional)
